status: Preregistered before any session of this version (2.0.0, home-screen candidate). Cases, rules and thresholds must not be changed after results are seen; a change requires a new protocol_version and new sessions.
reference_note: Targets are instructed fixation points shown to the participant. No independent eye tracker measures where the participant actually looked, so every spatial value is a target-referenced gaze error, not ground-truth eye-direction error.
hash_rule: Sessions record the SHA-256 of this file's bytes after converting CRLF to LF. The analyzer recomputes it the same way and rejects sessions whose hash differs.

primary.measured_output: The candidate's smoothed gaze coordinate: GazeSmoother output supplied to TrackerState.gaze and the overlay (columns smoothed_x_norm / smoothed_y_norm).
primary.predictor: Personal nine-point calibration GazeModel of the home-screen candidate, completed in the current tracking run; before the run starts the app refits GazeModel.fit on the frozen calibration inputs and requires identical parameters.

stages: cadence limiter: frames arriving within 66 ms of the previously accepted frame are skipped
MediaPipe Face Landmarker (VIDEO mode, one face)
LandmarkFeatures.extract: iris displacement in both eyes, nose position and eye-span scale (5 features), or a named rejection

GazeModel.predict: ridge-regularized linear map fitted by the nine-point calibration; null for non-finite features or when scale or face position left the calibration range; clamps each axis to [0, 1]
GazeSmoother: s + 0.28 * (p - s) per axis; a null prediction clears it
TrackerState.publish and DotOverlay (the smoothed coordinate, without a further rendering clamp)
pipeline.resets: The smoothing state is cleared by a null prediction, by the 800 ms no-result watchdog, and once at run start. A camera error hides the pointer but does not clear the smoothing state; it is logged as an event.
pipeline.not_part_of_this_pipeline: No stale-result rule, no eye-state classifier, no head-pose correction, no pretrained model, no click, scroll, dictation or cloud features. The only dwell interaction (the post-calibration tutorial) is closed while the evaluation screen is shown.

live_preview.role: secondary; reported separately and never combined with blind results, because a visible pointer can change where the participant looks

initial.requirement: each session after a fresh nine-point calibration

collection_plan.additional_participants: Optional. Added later with this unchanged protocol; their sessions are appended, never overwriting earlier ones.
collection_plan.technical_pilot: Optional technical pilot before S1: participant IDs starting with 'PILOT' (for example PILOT01). Pilot sessions are imported only into data/pilot/ (gaze_eval_data.py import --allow-pilot), never into data/raw/, and are never official.

coordinates.frame: Full-display normalized coordinates in the candidate's calibration basis: x = screen_x_px / basis_width_px, y = screen_y_px / basis_height_px, where the basis is WindowManager.maximumWindowMetrics bounds (API 30+, which evaluation requires). Calibration anchors, evaluation targets and predictions all use this basis; a run is refused if the basis size or rotation differs from the calibration's.
coordinates.origin: Top-left of the display. Positive x = right, positive y = down.
coordinates.target_drawing: A target at (x, y) is drawn at view-local (x * basis_width - view_left, y * basis_height - view_top), the same mapping the calibration screen used for its anchors.
coordinates.linear_output: GazeModel linear map before the model's own [0, 1] clamp (columns linear_*). Diagnostic only: the app never uses it. It shows how often and how far the model clamp was active.
coordinates.predicted_output: GazeModel.predict output, clamped to [0, 1] per axis by the model (columns predicted_*).
coordinates.smoothed_output: GazeSmoother output (columns smoothed_*). Primary measured coordinate. It inherits the model clamp and can never leave [0, 1]; it is not an unclamped raw output.
coordinates.rendered_output: Screen pixels where DotOverlay draws the smoothed point (overlay view origin + smoothed x overlay view size; columns rendered_*_px). Empty when the pointer is hidden. Logged for reference only; never used for error metrics.

timing.order: Pass 1: serpentine from the top-left (even rows left to right, odd rows right to left). Pass 2: pass 1 reversed.
timing.assignment: Each processing attempt is assigned to a presentation and phase by its frame-acceptance timestamp (SystemClock.uptimeMillis) relative to the run start, never by the target on screen when its result arrives.
timing.clock: SystemClock.uptimeMillis (monotonic) for schedule, acceptance and result times; System.nanoTime (monotonic) for durations.
timing.frame_cadence: Frames arriving within 66 ms of the previously accepted frame are skipped by the candidate (at most about 15 accepted frames per second).
timing.run_start: The run clock starts 100 ms after the run screen is laid out; logging and the run_start smoothing reset happen before it. Results handled while a run is active but not logged as its attempts (frames in flight at run start) are dropped before smoothing and counted; such a frame accepted at or after the run start is a missing attempt and an integrity problem.

validity.valid_measurement_sample: A measurement-phase attempt with outcome 'processed', quality 'tracking' and finite smoothed x and y.
validity.invalid_attempts: Kept in availability accounting with their actual outcome (discarded_closing, discarded_model_changed, processing_error) or quality (no_features, prediction_rejected), with the candidate's own rejection names in feature_rejection / prediction_rejection. Excluded from spatial metrics; never imputed, carried forward or treated as zero error.
validity.off_screen: Smoothed coordinates cannot leave [0, 1] because GazeModel.predict clamps them. Their off-screen fraction is reported but is zero by construction and says nothing about overshoot; model_clamp_active_fraction (from the linear output) is reported as well.
validity.settling: Settling-phase attempts are excluded from spatial, availability and throughput metrics and reported separately.

data_sufficiency.purpose: Technical eligibility for diagnostic spatial summaries. Distinct from, and looser than, the performance pass conditions.
data_sufficiency.min_eligible_fraction_note: The p95-presentation-error and mean-jitter criteria are INSUFFICIENT_DATA when fewer than ceil(0.8 * planned) presentations are technically eligible (26 of 32). The fraction reuses the predeclared 0.80 successful-presentation rate.

performance_criteria.note: Predeclared Iteration 3 prototype engineering targets. They are not evidence of reliable small-button selection. Comparisons use unrounded values.

session_criteria.definition: Successful presentations / all planned presentations in the run (32).
Nearest-rank p95 (k = ceil(0.95 * n)) of the per-presentation mean errors of the smoothed coordinate of technically eligible presentations. Not a p95 across camera samples.
Mean over technically eligible presentations of sqrt(mean((x - mean_x)^2 + (y - mean_y)^2)) of valid smoothed coordinates.
Valid measurement attempts / all measurement-phase processing attempts. Undefined (INSUFFICIENT_DATA) when there are no attempts.
Valid measurement samples / planned measurement-window time of the run (32 x 1.5 s = 48 s). A window without attempts contributes zero samples.

Nearest-rank p95 of per-attempt processing latency over all run attempts with a measured latency, including invalid, stale and discarded results. Latency runs from frame acceptance for processing to publication (or explicit discard) of its result on the main thread. Not FaceLandmarker inference time alone, not physical eye-to-display latency, not dwell time.

metric_definitions.spatial_error_norm: e = sqrt((pred_x - target_x)^2 + (pred_y - target_y)^2) in full-display normalized units. Not a percentage of the screen diagonal and not a visual angle.
metric_definitions.spatial_error_px: e_px = sqrt(((pred_x - target_x) * display_width_px)^2 + ((pred_y - target_y) * display_height_px)^2).
metric_definitions.presentation_mean_error: Mean of the spatial errors of a presentation's valid measurement samples.
metric_definitions.session_mean_error: Mean of presentation mean errors; each technically eligible presentation weighted equally.
metric_definitions.jitter_rms: sqrt(mean((x - mean_x)^2 + (y - mean_y)^2)) within one presentation; pixel version scales dx by width and dy by height.
metric_definitions.bias: Signed mean of (pred - target) per axis per presentation; session value is the mean over eligible presentations. Positive x = right, positive y = down.
metric_definitions.off_screen_fraction: Valid measurement samples with a smoothed coordinate outside [0, 1] / all valid measurement samples. Zero by construction in this pipeline (model clamp).
metric_definitions.nearest_rank_p95: The k-th smallest value with k = ceil(0.95 * n), computed in integer arithmetic.
metric_definitions.model_clamp_active_fraction: Valid measurement samples whose linear model output is outside [0, 1] on either axis / all valid measurement samples. Diagnostic; shows how often the model clamp changed the prediction.

statuses.MET: The criterion was measured and satisfied its threshold.
statuses.NOT_MET: The criterion was measured and failed its threshold.
statuses.NOT_MEASURED: No session data exists for the criterion yet.
statuses.INSUFFICIENT_DATA: Data exist but are too few, or fail an integrity check, to evaluate the criterion.
statuses.INCOMPLETE: The session ended before all presentations were shown; it cannot receive a passing verdict.

assertions: Invalid or insufficient presentations cannot be successful presentations.
Missing coordinates never become zero error.
An incomplete session's verdict is INCOMPLETE, whatever its partial metrics.
A session with logging loss, unassigned rows or a checksum mismatch has verdict INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
A session verdict is MET only if every session criterion is MET.
Session p95 values are never averaged; a participant-level p95 is recomputed from pooled presentation means.

aggregation.session: All criteria are evaluated per session.
aggregation.participant: Within one compatibility group, using complete sessions only. Verdict MET only if every included session verdict is MET; NOT_MET if any is NOT_MET; INCOMPLETE if no complete session exists; otherwise INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Descriptive participant metrics weight presentations equally (successful-presentation rate, pooled-presentation p95, mean jitter) or sessions equally (availability, valid sample rate); latency is reported as the worst session p95, never as an averaged p95.
aggregation.compatibility_group: Sessions are only summarized together when pipeline variant, mode, protocol hash, build commit and dirty flag, predictor kind, device model and display size and rotation all match. Sessions of protocol 1.0.0 (integrated main pipeline, log schema 2) are never pooled with this version.
aggregation.frame_weighting: No summary weights sessions by camera frame count.

changes: Measured output is the candidate's smoothed coordinate, which inherits GazeModel's [0, 1] clamp, instead of the unclamped GazeSample.point.
Predictor stages are the candidate's: 5 features, GazeModel with its pose/scale validity rules, 0.28 exponential smoothing.
Invalid-attempt categories are the candidate's actual outcomes; stale_delivery, discarded_epoch and eye-state qualities do not exist in this pipeline.
Calibration inputs are frozen from memory (the candidate keeps no saved calibration); verification refits GazeModel.fit on them.
Frame cadence is the candidate's 66 ms instead of 33 ms; the run clock starts 100 ms after layout; results in flight at run start are dropped and counted.
Rendering stage is the candidate overlay, which has no rendering clamp.

Unchanged: grid, 32 cases and their order, 80 s schedule, 1,000 ms settling and 1,500 ms measurement windows, treatment of missing coordinates, data sufficiency, all thresholds, metric formulas and aggregation rules.
